Lih Pao ( 立報 ) dated Jan.27:

STUDENTS CREATE DISTURBANCES IN WESTERN DISTRICT

The other day about 20 groups of students
delivered lectures among the people in the vicinity of Zau
Ka Doo ( 曹家渡 ), Jessfield Road, Robison Road and in
Chapei. The lecturers also distributed handbills
and posted slogans along the streets.
At 7 a.m. January 26 in the vicinity of Robison
and Kiaochow Roads, 19 persons, including 5 girls, were
arrested. Most of them were students of the Ai Chun
( 愛羣 ) Girls School, the Chinan ( 暨南 ) and other
universities.
Upon learning of this, the students giving
lectures in Chapei together with a number of factory
workers in the vicinity of Robison Road, in all about some
600 persons, called at the Zau Ka Doo Branch of the Public
Safety Bureau at 1 p.m. the same day and submitted the
following demands:-
1) That the arrested students be released.
2) That the students' patriotic movement be protected.
3) That the persons responsible for the assault on students
be punished.
Colonel Tan Pao Zeu ( 譚葆壽 ), Chief of the
Branch Bureau, who received them, stated that the 6th
Branch Bureau had not despatched any policemen to arrest
students. This statement was not believed by the
people who insisted on searching the premises of the Branch
Bureau.
The people and the students rushed into the
Branch Bureau and as only 20 policemen were stationed in
the Bureau, Colonel Tan ordered non-resistance, as a
result of which two of the policemen were assaulted and
injured. Many windows were smashed by the people.
As none of the arrested students were found on
the premises, the people took Colonel Tan out of the Branch
Bureau and marched off with him towards the Woo Kwoh Zang
( 五角場 ), Jessfield Road. Colonel Tan later effected
his escape to the Pao Kong Ziang ( 宝康祥 ) Cigarette
Shop, No.1258 Jessfield Road, but the crowd shouting
"assault him" went into the shop and assaulted Colonel
Tan who was slightly injured, despite the efforts of some
of the students of Chinan University to make the people
desist.
In the meantime, four police vans of Bubbling
Well Station had arrived and the Settlement Police dispersed
the crowd and effected the release of Colonel Tan who
was later escorted to Bubbling Well Station in a police
van.
During the disturbances Chen Yoeh Ching ( 陳玉卿 ),
Chinese policeman No.2503 of Bubbling Well Station, was
deprived of his pistol.
Upon being informed of the disturbances, the
Headquarters of the Public Safety Bureau detailed two
squads of policemen to various points in Zau Ka Doo.
Detectives and policemen of the Settlement Authorities
also rendered assistance.

Ta Mei Wan Pao reproduced the following article from the
Ta Kung Pao of Tientsin :-
THE REPERCUSSIONS OF THE STUDENTS GATHERING AT NANKING
The gathering of representatives of students
and principals of schools throughout the country, which
was held at Nanking on January 15 is an unprecedented event
not only in the political history of China but also in
the history of the students' movement in our country.
There is no doubt that this assembly has had considerable
and profound repercussions upon the political administration
and cultural understanding of our country.
We give below an analysis of these repercussions:-
In the first place, the convocation of this
gathering was due chiefly to the students' movement for
the preservation of the country, a movement which has

3.
January 23, 1936. Morning Translation.

propagated and developed during the whole of the last
month. The despair and anxiety of the youths over the
existing political situation was the principal and essential
cause of this movement. In fact, ever since the September
18th Incident, the Central Government has frequently
declared that it had already decided upon a definite plan
to deal with foreign affairs, but this plan was never
announced. In the meantime our territory has been invaded
inch by inch and Japanese aggression has been intensified
to such a point that it was not surprising that the Hopei
and Charhar Incidents had arisen. In their despair over
the policy of Government, the majority of the students
were compelled to resort to a movement such as that which
was launched last month to deal with present events.
We are convinced that the students'
movement is a noble movement. The Government should dispel
all causes for misunderstanding with a view to giving
full satisfaction to the representatives of the students
so that they can rely upon the Government in all foreign
affairs.
In the second place, the students' movement
may be said to have been due to the fact that the students'
plan for the preservation of the country was of an extremist
nature and was opposed by the Government leaders who desired
to maintain the status quo. The telegrams and the letters
which were dispatched by the Students Federations were
intended to urge the Government to adopt a strong policy
when dealing with foreign affairs. The youths to-day
are doing their utmost, whilst the grown-ups are cool.
The only thing for us to do is to decide upon a plan which
will enable us to obtain results, but this requires
courage. The Central Government has, on the one hand,
decided upon a definite plan which will enable it to attain
its aim for national salvation, while, on the other, it
has manifested its sincerity by inviting the students to
reveal their complaints.
In the third place, the students, during
the past years, have been deprived of freedom of assembly
in their schools. This act of oppression was frequently
carried out by the principals of the schools despite the
justification of the demand made by the students. The
students' movement which developed rapidly this time in
spite of all restrictions is the direct consequence of
a former reaction. The traditional respect of students
towards teachers disappeared a long time ago. At the
present time, the students can organize federations since
the Government has asked for their views as regards the
preservation of the nation. The foolish actions of the
principals of the schools have been counteracted, thereby
enabling the political and cultural administration of our
country to enter upon a new phase.

China Times published the following editorial on January 16 :-

SOME QUESTIONS FOR STUDENTS.

In reply to a summons from General Chiang Kai Shek, President of the Executive Yuan, representatives of university and secondary school principals and students from every part of the country are now at Nanking to express their views on the salvation of the country and at the same time to hear an explanation of the policy of the government in the present situation.

This meeting, which is bringing together the government leader, the tutors and the future masters of the country in a hall to exchange views on national salvation and reconstruction, is not to be regarded as an ordinary affair.

While this meeting of students is taking place in Nanking, we wish to say a few words to their representatives :-

(1) What is the cause of the national crisis?
(2) Why has the situation become aggravated since the September 18 Incident?
(3) What is the cause of the Shanghai and Tangku Pacts and their consequences?
(4) Why does China waver between an attitude of peace and war? What will be the consequences of peace and war?
(5) If the students were in the place of the government leaders, what would they desire the people to do?
(6) Why have Cheng Hsiao Su and Ying Ju Keng, who had received a high education, become traitors?

If the students' representatives can reply to these questions, they will be able to explain these questions to their comrades on their return from Nanking, otherwise their trip to the Capital would have been fruitless.

CHIANG KAI SHEK RECEIVES REPRESENTATIVES OF STUDENTS

At 2.30 p.m. January 16 the 300 representatives
of presidents, principals and students of colleges and
high schools of various places gathered at the Officers
Moral Endeavour Association (勵志社 ) to attend the
giving of instructions by General Chiang Kai Shek, President
of the Executive Yuan. The Minister and the Vice
Minister of Education, the officials of the Reception
Office etc. were in attendance.
At 3 p.m. General Chiang Kai Shek arrived at
the Association. Following an address made by Wong Shih
Chih (王世杰), Minister of Education, General Chiang
Kai Shek delivered a speech the main points of which were:-
1) The international situation during the past few years
and the diplomatic negotiations between China and
Japan are known to all.
2) The Government will not conclude any agreement that
impairs the territorial integrity and the sovereign
rights of China, nor will it make any secret pact.
The people may rest assured of this.
3) The strength of a nation depends upon its culture
and economics. All school principals and students
should observe discipline and accept full responsibility
for the fate of the country. They should not be led
astray by others into damaging school premises and
committing breaches of the peace and order. The
national crisis will pass if the people throughout
the country will remain faithful to the country and
conduct orderly struggles.

entertained to dinner at the Officers Moral Endeavour
Association by the Minister of Education who gave an
explanation of the following points:-
1) The educational policy during this extraordinary period.

and schools established by the Government at Tientsin
and Peiping.
3) The rumoured revision of textbooks.

Shun Pao (Swatow Correspondence) -

THE ACTIVITIES OF RONINS IN SOUTH CHINA

At 4 p.m. January 4, a boat laden with over one hundred bales of smuggled rice and beans was discovered near Chaoyang. The boat was taken to the wharf of the Teh Kee Company at Swatow and officers were detailed by the Smuggling Prevention Bureau to supervise the unloading of the rice and beans. In the evening more than ten ronins, armed with knives and axes, appeared at the wharf and assaulted the inspectors. They then cut the ropes of the boat with the intention of removing the vessel, but were prevented by the inspectors. The Bureau, upon being notified, sent fifty armed policemen who dispersed the ronins. All the smuggled goods in the boat were eventually taken to a granary.
On the following morning a certain ronin, claiming to be the owner of the smuggled goods, called on Siao Sung Zee, Director of the Bureau, and made several unreasonable demands. Lee Yoh Kun, a Staff Officer, and Lee Yuan Ho, the Mayor, were informed and they in turn made a report to the Kwangtung Provincial Government requesting the early return to Swatow of one Lee Han Vung to handle the affair.

Ta Lei Wan Pao dated January 10 :-

AGITATION AGAINST THE AUTONOMOUS MOVEMENT IN NORTH CHINA

Manifesto issued by the Shanghai University Professors
National Salvation Federation

In view of the grave crisis which is confronting China at present, more than sixty local professors, including Koo Ling (顾孟余) and Sung Chung Shih (宋仲石) recently formed the Shanghai University Professors National Salvation Federation and decided to support the patriotic movement launched by the students in various parts of the country.

On January 9, the Federation issued the following manifesto:-

"At the present time when foreign aggression is penetrating deeper and deeper into the interior of China, the people started extensive movements for national salvation. In our patriotism we make the following suggestion:-

(1) The ambitious designs of Japan in encroaching upon China are becoming increasingly outrageous. Japan desires to annex the whole of China. Ever since the September 18th Incident, our Government has repeatedly announced its policy of prolonged resistance. Now is the time for us to put up a resistance. During the past month, troops of the 'puppet state' have invaded Chahar, while the traitors in Luantung have occupied Tangku. This is indeed a trick of playing Chinese against Chinese. Should the Chinese troops in North China turn to the enemy and act as their vanguard against us, will our Government be in a position to maintain the territorial integrity of China? We should urge our Government not to lose this opportunity to put up a final resistance. As the entire Chinese nation have demonstrated their determination to fight Japan, the Government should observe the wishes of the people.

(2) The national spirit of the people constitutes the strongest support to the diplomacy of our country. The action of the traitorous elements in Peiping and Tientsin in establishing a bogus autonomous organization has stirred up the indignation of the students in Peiping and Tientsin and they have held demonstrations and submitted appeals. Similar activities were immediately followed in other parts of the country. The traitors then resorted to the spreading of rumours. If our Government will sincerely follow the principles of revolutionary diplomacy, it should immediately accord protection to the patriotic movements of the people and should devise means to extend the sphere of the students movement so as to improve their organization. If the Government will only decide to put up a resistance, all the students throughout the country will offer their lives on the battle field and become martyrs for the preservation of the nation. We therefore urge government officials to refrain from curbing the national spirit of the people as a way to please the enemy and not to oppress students as a way to encourage the underhand activities of traitorous elements."

November 18, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pao published the following telegrams from
Tientsin on November 17 :-

GENERAL DOIHARA DIRECTS THE AUTONOMOUS MOVEMENT IN
NORTH CHINA

According to information from a reliable
source, General Doihara of the Japanese Kwantung Army on
November 7 submitted a demand to General Sung Cheh Yuan,
the Garrison Commander of Peiping and Tientsin, requesting
him to proceed with the movement for an autonomy in North
China, within three days. General Sung, however, replied
that this cannot be decided on, until the 5th National
Congress of the Kuomintang, at present being held in
Nanking, is over.
It is said that the various offices of
the National Government in North China, including the
Peiping Military Council, will be abolished while a new
organ will be established with General Sung Cheh Yuan as
the leader. The new organ will, however, maintain some
adequate connections with the National Government. This
is the fundamental scheme of the formation of an autonomous
government in North China but whether the National
Government will accept it or not is at present unknown.
The above information has been released by
Japan and is reported to have been confirmed by the
Chinese authorities.
It is further reported that the Customs
revenue, the Salt revenue, Consolidated Tax, Stamp Tax,
and other government revenues of North China will be with-
held for the development of North China.
General Doihara is intending to make North
China entirely independent from the National Government
and proposes that the suggested autonomous government
adopts a new emblem and new coins. General Sung Cheh
Yuan, however, is insisting that (1) the new government
should be under the National Government in its organization
and (2) the integrity of North China should be preserved;
none of North China should be annexed by Japan or "Manchukuo".
According to general observation, the "connections" between
the suggested autonomous government and the National
Government may be cut off at a time when the National
Government may be alleged to have undertaken anti-Japanese
activities.
General Sung Cheh Yuan held that this
movement should not be carried until the time is opportune
and has requested Japan accordingly. The latter, however,
is exerting every effort to press Sung.
The so-called new state of North China
would consist of Hopei, Chahar, Suiyuan, Shansi and
Shantung Provinces. It has not been definitely decided
however, whether or not the two last named provinces will
be included.

The Shanghai Cultural Circles' National Salvation

4) That a demand be made for the immediate despatch of

5) That armed resistance to the enemy's invasion be demanded.
6) That all traitors be severely punished and their
properties confiscated.
"These proposals are supported by educated
circles and the people generally, yet they have not been
adopted by our Government. The autonomous movement in
North-China has been given the name of Hopei-Charhar
Political Commission. This bogus commission is still
extending its organization and territory, and the six
hsiens in East Charhar have fallen under bombardment by

THE RENT REDUCTION MOVEMENT

In view of the fact that the numerous
petitions submitted to the local Tangpu and other political
organs for a general reduction in house rents
have had no result, the Shanghai Municipal Rent Reduction
Committee has decided to convene a joint meeting of
representatives of the various branch rent reduction
associations at 2 p.m. January 8 to discuss definite
measures to be taken.
Yesterday the Committee sent another
appeal to the local Tangpu, the Shanghai City Government,
the City Government Council and various other Government
organs requesting assistance.
The following is an abridged translation
of the appeal:-
"Ever since the January 28th Incident,
the business of industrial and commercial enterprises in
Shanghai has been seriously affected. Numerous shops
have closed, while the number of unemployed is daily
increasing, and many of them, unable to find a decent
means to earn a living, have resorted to crime.
"Although two years have elapsed since
petitions were submitted for a general reduction in house
rents, no official mandate for a reduction has been issued.
Local citizens desire a reduction in house rents, but
they have no alternative but to suspend the payment of
house rents in the hope of making the landlords give a
voluntary reduction. Landlords, however, are suing tenants
in Court for payment of rent; many shops have been sealed
up. Unless immediate relief be given, conditions will
become very grave. We, therefore, submit you this petition
with a request that you will immediately issue an official
decree ordering a general reduction in house rents so as to
alleviate the burden of the people."

THE TRUE FACTS OF THE AUTONOMY MOVEMENT

It is known to all that the so-called
autonomous movement in North China was started under the
false claim that it is the people's wish, but in reality
it was at the instigation of a certain nation which is
planning to establish a second puppet state. With this
object in view, it is doing its best to frustrate the
efforts of our government to readjust the internal
administration of the country.
When General Ho Ying Chin left for
the North, the Tokyo "Asahi Shimbun" alleged that the
General's presence in the North would aggravate the
situation. What Japan's real motive is we are not in
a position to say, but her protest against General Ho's
departure for Northern China constitutes an
interference with the domestic affairs of China and
obstructs the enforcement of her administrative power
within her own territory. Japan has informed Great
Britain and the United States that she will not interfere
with the People's Autonomous Movement in North China,
which is a purely Chinese domestic affair, but she has
intimated that she will not remain indifferent if it
affects the interests of peace in China, Japan, or
'Manchukuo', should the Chinese Government adopt forcible
measures to suppress this movement. In other words,
Japan is prepared to protect this movement by resorting
to military force. This shows that the relations between
Japan and the autonomous movement are the same as those
between a nursemaid and a child.
The proclamation of the autonomous
movement which bears the significance of foreign
instigation is intended for the purpose of partitioning
Chinese territory, reducing the efforts of the Chinese
national unification and accelerating the crisis for the
annihilation of the Chinese race. What the traitorous
elements care most about is how to please Japan.
With a view to safeguarding the puppet
state in Manchuria, Japan must first annihilate Chinese
influence from North China, and in order to secure
Mongolia, Japan must seize privileges for her free move-
ments in North China. If Japan desires to monopolize
the financial market in North China, she must first
secure the control of the political administration in
that territory. Being anxious to attain these objects,
Japan has resorted to all sorts of aggression and coercion.
Ever since June last, the situation
in North China has become increasingly tense. The
dissolution of the Tangpu and the withdrawal of the
government troops from the district were all due to the
Japanese oppression and coercion. However, despite all
this, the traitors in North China were rendered powerless
to extend their underhand activities, as the government
officials and the civilians in North China were all on
the alert. These traitors therefore started the bogus
autonomous movement under the false pretence of acceding

The Students Movement in Peiping

Meanwhile over 180 professors in
Peiping have issued a joint manifesto denouncing this
movement. Some 4,000 students of the universities of
Peiping started demonstrations and held processions on
the morning of December 9 in protesting against the
establishment of a bogus autonomous organization in North
China by some disgruntled politicians under the pretext
of pleasing the public. They have made the following
demands:-
(1) To preserve the political administration and territorial
sovereignty of China.
(2) To protest against the separation of Chinese territory.
(3) To protest against secret diplomacy and to demand
the publication of the diplomatic negotiations between
China and Japan.
(4) To demand the freedom of assembly,
speech, publications and patriotic movements.
(5) To cease all civil wars immediately.
(6) To protest against the arrest of civilians at will.
(7) To demand the immediate release of the arrested students.
Such an unanimous demonstration of

The so-called North China Question

and the perseverance of the entire Chinese nation to
overcome the intrigues of our aggressor.

Mayor Wu Teh Chen's Open Letter To The Students.

With the return of the entire body of the student
petitionists last night, Mayor Wu Teh Chen issues the
following open letter addressed to the students :-
"As a result of the earnest advice given by the
government and local educational authorities, the entire
body of the local students, who attempted to proceed to
Nanking to submit an appeal, returned to Shanghai from Wusih
at 3 p.m. yesterday. I cannot suppress my feelings of joy
at your return.
"When you gathered around the Shanghai North
Station and occupied the trains with the object of submitting
an appeal, did you ever give a thought to the bad atmosphere
prevailing over Shanghai at that time? The public is in
sympathy with your patriotism, but in view of the difficulties
now confronting China and the much complicated condition in
Shanghai, reactionary elements attempt to take advantage of
the situation to create disturbances. On the day following
your gathering at the North Station, a crowd of about 4000
persons assembled and simultaneously reactionary handbills
made their appearance. A crowd of 1000 persons gathered
along Paoshan Road ready to start trouble in an attempt to
cause a tragic incident. In view of the trying situation,
I made every effort to persuade a portion of the students
to return to their schools, whilst for your safety sake I
was compelled to order the train to leave the station.
"Upon your departure westward, I immediately
detailed responsible officials to come forward to take care
of you and at the same time I asked the principals of various
schools to assist in the persuasion. I was worried all day
long over your conditions. Fortunately, the students of the
Tungchi University came back on December 25, whilst the entire
body returned yesterday afternoon. Although your train has
not reached Nanking, yet your wishes have already been conveyed
by me and have even been accepted by the National Government.
Since you have returned, you must henceforth restrain your-
selves and wait for the moment when you can offer practical
service to the government.
"I need not repeat my views about how the youths
of to-day should serve their country, as I explained to you
in my statement on December 21. If we have an actual and deep
understanding of the present national difficulties, we shall
realize that to serve the country in a true spirit does not
constitute merely a moment's indignation but an everlasting
struggle. We must not be misled by our feelings and we must
not mistake the outside appearance as the practical one.
During the past national salvation movements, there has
always existed one very sad factor, that is to say, the misuse
of our energy. Such will not prove of any value in the
alleviating of our national crisis, and it will only do harm
to the community. It is much to be deplored by those who love
their country with true spirit. China will become a strong
nation only when our awakening youths realize the real cause
of their national crisis, concentrate their energy to serve
their country in a body, and under the leadership of the
Central Government, struggle for the existence of their nation.
In this manner only will it be possible to bring back ever-
lasting glory to our nation.
"I hope you will pay heed to my views."

The Mass Livelihood(大众生活), a weekly periodical, published
the following article on December 21 :-

ARE PEIPING AND TIENTSIN STILL UNDER CHINA'S JURISLICTION?

I think the Chinese masses living outside
Peiping and Tientsin will regard me as a madman for asking
such a question: "Are Peiping and Tientsin still under
China's jurisdiction?"
To-day, military aeroplanes that are not of
Chinese ownership are daily flying over Peiping and Tientsin,
and in the latter district a large military aerodrome,
occupying a piece of land measuring about 1,000 mow, is
under construction. As I have not been to foreign countries,
I cannot say whether the flying of Chinese military aeroplanes
in Great Britain, America or Japan would be permitted. My
common sense tells me that if Peiping and Tientsin are still
Chinese territory, China should not allow such activities.
Reports have been constantly appearing in the
newspapers that the government of a "friendly nation", in
order to protect the safety of North China, is opposed to
the troops of the Chinese Government proceeding to the North
because of a certain treaty. At present, large numbers of
soldiers of the "friendly nation" have concentrated in Peiping
and Tientsin.
I personally witnessed the autonomous movement
in Tientsin. On a certain morning I saw 10 trucks, carrying
a large number of ragged drug addicts, some in military
uniforms, appear on a thoroughfare in a certain Concession
of Tientsin. I at first thought that these drug addicts
were under arrest. Two hours later rumours were prevalent
and "extras" were on sale. I bought a copy and on reading it
I learnt that these drug addicts were dare-to-die represen-
tatives who were on their way to the City Government to
demand autonomy and ready to take over the administration.
Such a state of affairs exists not only in
Peiping and Tientsin, but also in the demilitarized zones in
East Hopei which are at present forcibly occupied by the
rebel Yin Zu Keng and which have openly seceded from Nanking.
Of late, groups of "xx" soldiers, fully armed, could be seen
everyday visiting various Hsiens throughout the province of
Hopei, conducting surveys everywhere. These soldiers even
force the inhabitants to sign pro-autonomy manifestoes which
they carry with them already prepared, and those who refuse
to comply with their order are instantly shot to death.
Some time ago, our government officials
declared that no loss of China's sovereign rights would
be tolerated and that they would not yield. But do not
the present conditions in Hopei constitute loss of sovereign
rights to China? Do not the changes that have taken
place in North China indicate that the moment has come for
sacrifices?

The China Sketch (中國 sketch ), Volume 5, published the
following article :- (Abbreviated Translation)

THE NORTH CHINA QUESTION

The Chinese people are paying close
attention to the autonomous movement in North China and
the activities of the shameless traitor Yin Ju Keng.
It is known to all who is at the back of these activities.
It is said that as soon as the North China Question
has been settled, China will have no other vital problems
to be solved. Such a statement will obscure public
understanding of this important question in which the
life or death of the Chinese race is bound up. We warn
the Chinese people that our most vital problem to-day
is the preservation of the Chinese race.
In the beginning the North-Eastern
Question appeared to have no connection with other parts
of China. When China's North-Eastern territory was
lost, it seemed that the affair was closed. It was not
believed at the time that the loss of the North-East
was the commencement of the collapse of the whole
of China, and would eventually develop into a problem
affecting the very existence of the Chinese race. Facts
have now proved that this belief was absolutely wrong.
We are strongly opposed to the
autonomous government instigated by the enemy. If this
movement can be suppressed temporarily, could it be
said to have settled the North China Question? Even
if there had been no movement for self-government, could
any piece of territory in which Chinese troops are not
allowed free movement, and Chinese officials and civilians
can be arrested at will, be regarded as a part of China?
There are many methods of aggression, such as by
economic rapprochement, cultural co-operation, etc.
We should not allow ourselves to be deceived but we
should pay careful attention to the fact that even a
settlement of the dispute would not give practical
benefits, but would on the contrary give rise to endless
trouble.

THE STUDENTS PATRIOTIC MOVEMENT

The students movement which has been quiet for
a long time is being revived. Although the movement
cannot remedy the situation in North China, it shows
that the spirit of the Chinese people is still active.
We are in full sympathy with the students.

NANCHI

ATTEMPTED SUICIDE OF A JAPANESE

A Japanese named Tokuichi Sakai, aged 58,
of Nagasaki arrived in Shanghai on December 21, and stayed
at the Yamato Hotel. On December 22 he removed to No. 23
Nanking Road, the home of Mr. K. Yamanaka. At about 11 p.m.
December 22, Sakai left the house saying that he had some
engagement. At 1 a.m. December 23, the local Japanese
Consular Police received a report from the Purser of the
S.S. "Kazan Maru" that he had saved a Japanese who had
attempted to commit suicide. Sakai was taken to the
Consulate, where it was revealed that he had jumped into
the river to commit suicide but was picked up by the crew
of a launch and then removed to the "Kazan Maru". Mr.
Yamanaka was ordered to appear before the Consular Police.
It is believed that Sakai is mentally deranged.

NIPPO

THE CHINESE STUDENTS MOVEMENT

The Chinese students movement has been
intensified. A characteristic of the present movement
is that the students of mission schools maintained by
British and Americans, especially those of the latter,
are taking a prominent part. This is a reflection of the
British and American attitude towards autonomy of North
China. As professors of universities seem to be instigating
the movement, developments are being carefully watched.
It is a fact that politicians who had failed to secure
office in the newly organized Chinese Government are
encouraging the movement behind the scenes.
As it is feared that these activities
may develop into an anti-Government and anti-Chiang Kai Shek
movement, the Nanking Government will adopt suppressive
measures.

The anti-autonomous movement of the
students which has spread throughout China is being
regarded by the Nanking Government as a patriotic movement,
therefore the Chinese Authorities are not suppressing it.
Recent developments indicate that the movement is being
secretly instigated from behind by third parties and
radical elements and communists. It has, therefore, been
decided to summon to Nanking the Presidents of universities
at various places and to give them instructions regarding
the policy to be adopted in directing the students.
Representatives of students will also
be summoned to Nanking before January 15 next year when
General Chiang Kai Shek will personally warn them not to
act thoughtlessly.

GENERAL CHIANG KAI SHEK TO SUMMON PRESIDENTS OF UNIVERSITIES

        On December 23, General Chiang Kai Shek,
President of the Executive Yuan, issued the following
order to the Ministry of Education:-
        "The situation of China has been critical
for the past years and the National Government is doing
its best in an endeavour to combat the danger.  Leaders
of the educational circles well understand the existing
situation of the nation and they should transmit their
knowledge to the people.  With a view to making people
of the educational circles become more aware of the
national position, the Ministry of Education should fix
a date on which to call a meeting at Nanking of the
principals of the colleges and higher institutions from
all the provinces and the cities under the direct
control of the Executive Yuan, where communication is
convenient, (or of deans or important teachers of colleges
and higher institutions as representatives) and of the
principals of middle schools (at most five principals
of middle schools may attend from each province or city)
so that they may learn the policies of the government
and offer their views".
        The Executive Yuan at the same time issued
another order to the Ministry of Education as follows:-
        "The government is willing to announce its
policy towards the national affairs and is particularly
willing to consider and accept the views of the youths.

three students of every college or important higher
institution in all provinces and cities under the
direct control of the Executive Yuan, where communication
is convenient, to come to Nanking in company with the
principal concerned on January 15, 1936, when the
President of the Yuan will give an explanation of the

meeting".

Futan University Students Refuse to Leave North Station

At 10.30 a.m. yesterday more than
300 students of the Futan University proceeded on foot
to the North Station from their school, proposing to
board trains to Nanking for the purpose of submitting
appeals. Li Dah Chao (李大超), Head of the First
Department of the Shanghai City Government, in conjunction
with Huang Chun Poh (黄君復), Chief of the Branch
Bureau of Public Safety at the Civic Centre, tried in
vain to dissuade them. The students reached the North
Station at 12.45 p.m. Later they all boarded the train
which was scheduled to leave the Station for Nanking
at 1.20 p.m. However, the railway authorities were
instructed not to despatch the train. Although repeated
negotiations were opened with the students, no result
was attained.

During the time when the students
were on the way to the North Station, the police of the
Bureau of Public Safety put up temporary barbed wire
barriers on Ziang Ying Road (翔殷路) and at the corner
of Paoshan and Jukong Roads. They also closed the iron
gates at Paoshan Road (Shanghai-Woosung Station) and
the gates of the North Station in the hope of obstructing
the advance of the students. However all this was of
no avail and eventually the students reached the North
Station. A large number of police and also members of
the Peace Preservation Corps were posted around the
vicinity of the North Station for the purpose of
maintaining order. They advised the students to leave
on the buses and motor cars belonging to the City Government
stationed in front of the North Station, but the students
refused to go.

At about 3.30 p.m. Dr. T.H. Lee (李登辉),
Director of the Futan University, arrived at the North
Station with Chin Tung Ying (金通尹), Chief Secretary,

but without avail.

From 1 p.m. yesterday till mid night,
no trains left the Station, while those which arrived
from Nanking and Hangchow were stopped at Markham Road
Station and the Shanghai South Station.

and forcibly occupied trains, thereby obstructing traffic

Trouble on Nanking Road

At 8.30 a.m. yesterday the Central Police Station in the International Settlement received secret information to the effect that a large number of students would visit Nanking to disseminate handbills and deliver open air lectures.

Fearing that the presence of these students may affect peace and order in the Settlement, a large group of detectives and policemen, led by Chinese and foreign inspectors, were detailed to patrol on Nanking Road.

Later, about 500 to 600 students and people were noticed gathering in the vicinity of the Continental Emporium near the corner of Shantung Road. The students distributed handbills. With a view to preventing incidents, the police inspectors and their subordinates peacefully persuaded the crowd to disperse, but without result. Then the Police dispersed them and some trivial trouble arose. Inspector Watson was injured in the face, Inspector Furness was hurt in the arm and face, Inspector West was injured in the face, while his helmet was damaged.

Tong Tsoong Hsiang (董崇湘), a student of Medhurst College, and Dzung Chu Wei (鄭樹慰), an exchange broker, were arrested on the spot. Order on Nanking Road was not resumed until after 11 a.m.

The two arrested persons were taken before the First Special District Court at 12.30 p.m. where they were charged with obstructing public officers in the execution of their duties (Article 135 and 136 of the Chinese Criminal Code). Inspectors Watson, Furness and West gave evidence.

After they had been interrogated by Judge Tan (戴), the two accused were sentenced to 3 months' imprisonment each, with suspension for three years. The accused were ordered to furnish shop security in case they desired to appeal.

The two accused were then taken to the Security Department of the Court. They will be set free as soon as the necessary security has been furnished.

At the time when the trouble occurred, Dzung Chu Wei was slightly injured in the head. Thus his head was bound with white cloth.

Students Leave North Station

At noon December 23, some 300 students of Futan University congregated at the North Station with the intention of taking trains to Nanking to submit appeals to the authorities. Despite every persuasion by the authorities and the President of the University to induce them to return to their school, the students refused to move and remained at the Station. Furthermore, the students assaulted and injured several unarmed policemen and also distributed reactionary handbills.

December 25, 1935. Morning Translation.

On the morning of December 24, a number of middle school students, instigated by elements of the Communist Party and the Social Democratic Party, gathered in the compound of the Continental Emporium Building on Nanking Road and attempted to hold a procession in the Settlement. They distributed handbills of a reactionary character. These bad elements are planning to utilize the students to disturb the peace of this locality, to obstruct communications and to create a tragedy, thereby aggravating the situation. These elements even succeeded in entering the Settlement in the hope of giving rise to an international trouble.

At 2 p.m. yesterday, the Shanghai City Government notified the Presidents of the Universities concerned to gather at the North Station to advise their students to return to school. Students of the Chih Chih and other Universities complied with the advice to return, but several hundred students of Futan University, the Tung Chi University, the Chi Kuo Middle School and the Sz Pei Middle School refused to leave the North Station. As the North Station adjoins the Settlement, it is dangerous for the students to stay at the station. Trains were then prepared and the students were removed further inland.

It is reported that the Presidents of the Universities persuaded their students to continue their studies and to elect representatives to proceed to Nanking on January 15, 1936 in compliance with the instructions of General Chiang Kai Shek.

Middle schools will comply with the order of the Ministry of Education by commencing the winter vacation at an earlier date.

NICHI-NICHI

A BOMB EXPLOSION ON DARROCH ROAD

At 10.45 a.m. December 26, a Chinese second-hand goods hawker named Chen Ah Pao, aged 39, residing in Chapei, bought from two young ragpickers on Darroch Road an iron tin similar in shape to a cigarette tin for which he had paid 2 coppers. On finding that the tin contained a bomb the hawker was very pleased over the bargain. He placed the tin in one of the baskets which he was carrying. On arriving in front of the Kiyo Kan Hotel on Darroch Road he placed the baskets on the ground preparatory to taking a short rest. At this moment, the bomb exploded with a terrific noise. The hawker received serious injuries to his right thigh, while a Chinese boy named Wen Yung Fah, aged 17, residing at No. 1, Dong Foh Li, Jukong Road, was injured in the left leg. Chinese constable No. 30 of the East Wang Yang Road Station arrived at the scene immediately and sent for the Chapei ambulance.
The two injured persons were removed to Poo Tien Hospital on Hsin King Road where they were given first-aid treatment. The hawker was later removed to Lester Hospital as his injuries were very serious.
Police officers from Dixwell Road arrived at the scene and made an investigation. The Japanese Naval Landing Party also despatched a number of men and adopted precautionary measures.
At about 2 p.m. officers of the Public Safety Bureau took Wen Yung Fah to the scene of the explosion and carried out a reconstruction of the incident. An official of the Public Safety Bureau stated that owing to the serious condition of the hawker he could not be questioned so as to ascertain in what manner the bomb had come into his possession.

MANIFESTO OF THE SHANGHAI WOMEN'S NATIONAL
SALVATION FEDERATION

During the past four years our enemies have seized
four provinces in the North-East and massacred large
number of our countrymen. They are continuing to oppress
us and have now commenced to attack North China. First of
all they utilized the traitor Ying Ju-keng and established
the "East Hopei Anti-Communist Committee," and then they
instigated numerous traitors to "sell" our national rights
under the pretext of promoting an autonomy movement. In
reality Hopei and Chahar now exist in name only and hundreds
of thousands of our countrymen in these provinces will soon
share the fate of our countrymen in the North-East (Manchuria)
and become slaves without a country.

The attack on North China is only a part of the plans
of our enemy and if we do not resist now, the whole of
China will fall into their hands. The North China
situation is actually a life-and-death problem for the
Chinese nation; it is certainly not a temporary or a non-
fundamental problem.

During this grave national crisis we can strive for
existence and independence only by struggling with our enemies
at the cost of our hot blood. Those of us who are vainly
begging our enemy for mercy by such methods as "Friendship"
and "Rapprochement" are slaves who will never awaken.

Take heed! the flame of patriotism in the hearts of
our countrymen is on the point of bursting forth. The
students in Peiping, foremost of all others, held parades

movements of the Peiping students. Since the men have
shown their spirit, how can we females remain within
doors waiting to be butchered by our enemies.

We call upon all women in Shanghai to unite and

AGITATION AGAINST THE AUTONOMOUS MOVEMENT IN NORTH CHINA.
Appeal Made By Students of Local Universities And Middle
Schools To The City Government.

At 4 p.m. December 19, about 6,000 students of the various local universities and middle schools assembled on the premises of the Chiaotung University and appointed their own presidium. At 9 p.m. they left the Chiaotung University and arrived at the Futan University at 3 a.m. December 20. Here they remained for some time, after which they continued their procession towards the Civic Centre, arriving there at about 5.30 a.m.

The students were received by Mayor Wu Teh Chen who earnestly advised them to observe strict order in their patriotic movements so as to avoid giving rise to other incidents that would only harass the Government in coping with the present difficulties. Mayor Wu also expressed his sincere desire that the students would not neglect their studies on account of their patriotic movement.

The students were greatly moved by Mayor Wu's speech. The presidium of the students then submitted to the Mayor a written petition containing the following seven demands :-
(1) That the Mayor be requested to send a telegram to the National Government requesting it to place a check on the oppression of the patriotic movement of the students by the military and political authorities in Peiping.
(2) That the National Government be requested to start a punitive campaign against the rebel, Yin Zu Keng, immediately.
(3) That the National Government be requested to protect the territorial integrity and sovereignty of China.
(4) That the National Government be requested to enforce a drastic revolutionary diplomacy.
(5) That the Mayor effect the immediate release of Lee Chung Sing(李震聲), a student of the Chiaotung University, who has been arrested.
(6) That the Mayor be requested to afford protection to the patriotic movement in Shanghai.
(7) That the National Government be requested to grant freedom of speech and assembly.

In reply, Mayor Wu said that he would afford every protection to the patriotic movement in Shanghai as long as it was conducted in an orderly manner. Mayor Wu added that Lee Chung Sing of the Chiaotung University had not been arrested and that he had only been summoned by the Public Safety Bureau simply for interrogation because he was under suspicion owing to the finding of a letter, and that he had been told to return to his school after interrogation. Mayor Wu promised to refer the other requests of the students to the National Government.

The students were satisfied with Mayor Wu's reply and dispersed at about 9 a.m. December 20.

COMMERCIAL CONCERNS NOT ALLOWED TO ACT AS SAVINGS BANKS

Information secured from the Shanghai Office
of the Ministry of Finance shows that the Ministry is
placing a strict control on savings banks as the existence
of the poor people of the community is to a large extent
dependent on their savings. Banks are not allowed to
indulge in savings business unless approval has been
obtained from the Ministry. Common commercial concerns,
however, absorb deposits daily under the false name of
savings; this is contrary to law. Furthermore, it is not
known how much capital these concerns have or what business
they do with the savings received. Poor people will
suffer considerably should these concerns lose money or
go bankrupt.
In 1930, the Ministry of Finance issued a
circular order to provincial and city governments in the
country notifying them to prohibit commercial concerns
from receiving deposits and doing savings business.
Reports have now been received that certain commercial
concerns are still receiving deposits. The Ministry of
Finance has now again instructed the provincial and city
governments repeating this order.

Preparations for demonstration by local students
against the autonomy movement in North China

During the afternoon of December 19 about 400 students
of the Chinan University held a meeting in the university
premises at Chenju in order to discuss the course of action
they should follow in connection with the conciliatory
attitude adopted by the National Government towards the
autonomy movement in the North. As a precautionary measure
against interference by the university authorities, the
students severed all the telephone connections and placed
pickets at the various entrances to prevent the teaching
staff from leaving. Resolutions were passed that a Chinan
University National Salvation Association be formed, and
that those present march to the Civic Centre, Kiangwan, to
stage a demonstration and submit the following five demands:-

2) That the students arrested in Peiping be released.
3) That the diplomatic negotiations being conducted by
the National Government be made public.
4) That an expedition be despatched to punish Ying Ju-keng,
the promoter of the autonomy movement.
5) That freedom of speech, press and organization be

ment in North China. After leaving the territory west of
the Settlement, the procession continued through Northern

Kiangwan, which was reached about 4 a.m. December 20.

December 20, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

The original purport of the Neutrality Law is to avoid America from being involved in a European war. America's imaginary enemy at present is not in Europe but in the Far East. At the time of the opening of the Naval Conference, America discovered a plan by which Japan would attempt to bombard her cities. Mr. Pittman, Chairman of the Diplomatic Commission, accused a certain nation in the Far East of being robbers. All this shows the deep concern displayed by the government and people of America over the question of Oriental Affairs as well as their hatred towards the aggressor. Should this Neutrality Law not be revised, then America will not be able to supply munitions to the oppressed nation. This will be contrary to America's policy and harmful to the world peace.

With the prospects of the Naval Conference gradually growing dim, the diplomatic relations between America and Japan are coming to an unprecedented crisis. America has made drastic preparations in her military affairs with the approach of the year 1936, but she is not yet ready diplomatically. The proposed revision of the Neutrality Law may be America's move to prepare herself diplomatically.

Chinese Saturday Post (礼拜六) published the following comment on December 14:-

OPPOSITION TO THE AUTONOMY IN THE NORTH

The establishment of the new political organization in the North, an autonomous form of political regime under disguise, is an expansion of the autonomy movement achieved by Yin Ju Keng. We must understand exactly how much our government had conceded and how disgraceful the surrender is. The so-called measures for the stability of the situation in North China discussed by and agreed upon between General Ho Yin Chin, who is responsible for conducting the negotiations over the North China problem, and General Sung Cheh Yuen, are really those that deprive the general public of their benefits. We do not know where the so-called suitable measures are that have been drawn up by our government, where the courage of General Ho Yin Chin is and how those political officers will be able to face the people who have been deceived and betrayed. The so-called "unification for the salvation of the nation" and the so-called "resistance against foreign insult" are all humbug.

The Hopei-Chahar Political Council is entirely an independent institution. In other words, these two provinces will be converted into a republic for the Japanese military base and traitors to occupy. The Sovereign Rights in these two provinces will not belong to China. The Chinese Government has had a previous example of such concessions and it can never be ensured that no further similar incidents will happen in South China or Central China. China as a consequence will be faced with ruin in the near future. The establishment of the new political regime in the North had secured approval from Doihara beforehand and all those pro-Japanese feudal elements were later invited to participate in the regime subject to the

The "Shanghai Party Voice" (上海党声), a weekly magazine,
dated Dec. 14:

SINO-JAPANESE RELATIONS IN NORTH CHINA.

Following the September 18 Incident, Japan seized
China's four North-eastern provinces, but yet she was not
contented. The Shanghai-Woosung Truce and the Tangku
Pact were concluded and still Japan thought that China
had not yet been humiliated to the extreme. So, she
instigated the creation of the so-called "Autonomy
Movement in North China."
Formerly, Japan was of the opinion that had she
not obtained Manchuria, she would be unable to exist, and
now she is claiming that the safety of Manchuria will not
be assured, if she does not secure North China. But, will
Japan remain calm and contented even when she possesses
North China? We expect to hear the words "The safety
of North China will not be possible if Japan cannot get
control of the Yangtse Valley" and finally we shall be
told that "the existence of the Japanese Imperial Empire
will not be secure, if Japan cannot get the whole of
China." Is it possible that Japan can win the hearts of
the Chinese people or the Government's endurance of insults
in this way? Such measures are not signs of "good
Sino-Japanese relations" or "rapprochement," but steps
adopted to destroy China and render her a second Liu Jeu
(琉球), Formosa, or Korea.
North China is the centre of Chinese culture
as well as the place where our Chinese race originated.
We are convinced that the four hundred million Chinese
people will offer all they have to assist the Government
if the latter will only take steps, no matter what they may
be, to protect North China. The Government has the
authority to order the people to be patient regarding the
North China affair or to call upon the people to sacrifice
themselves on account of the North China affair, as they wish.
Some time ago General Chiang Kai Shek, Chairman of
the Military Affairs Commission, announced that every effort
was to be made towards ensuring peace if there was a
possibility of bringing peace about. Now that there is
still a ray of hope for peace, it is time for the
Government to offer their final and best endeavours as well
as for the people to unite and to support the Government.
We can definitely say that the Chinese Government and its
people will pay great attention to this ray of hope for
peace, and use their best endeavours to succeed.

AGITATION AGAINST THE AUTONOMOUS MOVEMENT IN NORTH CHINA.

Futan University Students Make Appeal To The City Government.

At 2 p.m. yesterday, about 200 to 300 students of the Futan University marched in a body to the local City Government to submit an appeal. The procession was orderly. On the way the students shouted slogans: "Support the National Government", "Oppose the bogus autonomy in North China", etc. On arrival at the City Government, they stood in front of the building. They were received by Mayor Wu Teh Chen in person, to whom the students' representatives submitted an appeal in writing containing the following five requests :-
(1) That a telegram be sent asking the Peiping Authorities to release the arrested students and to issue compensation to wounded students.
(2) That protection be accorded to the students' patriotic movement.
(3) That severe punishment be meted out to military and police officers for having oppressed the movement conducted by the Peiping students.
(4) That the new organization in the disguise of autonomy in North China be opposed.
(5) That the National Government start a campaign against the rebels.

Mayor Wu replied to the five requests and also directed the students to strictly observe order and not to neglect their studies. The students were satisfied with Mayor Wu's reply and also took his advice, whereupon they left and returned to their school.

On their way back to their school, the students shouted the following slogans :-
(1) Support the National Government.
(2) Support the Chinese Kuomintang Party.
(3) Down with the bogus autonomy in North China.
(4) Assist our fellow students in Peiping.
(5) Demand protection for the students' patriotic movement.
(6) Demand the punishment of the military and police officers in Peiping for having caused the incident.
(7) Long live the Chinese Kuomintang Party.
(8) Long live the Chinese Republic.

"To-day the students of the Futan University in Shanghai make an appeal to this Government and demand that a telegram be sent asking you to release the arrested students and to accord medical treatment to those wounded students. Central China Daily News (Editorial):

NATIONAL SALVATION MOVEMENT

The national salvation movement originated
years and years ago. When a nation's existence is
at stake, her people will not remain silent or inconsiderate,
this being the natural sign to a nation of the development
of her people's rights.
Both China and her people were greatly
affected by the September 18 Incident and the January 28
War, and during the past four years, many hardships
have been encountered, but were eventually tided over.
During the past month, North China has been
in a state of crisis, and both the nation and her people
are facing a much more serious blow this time, when
they are actually striving for their existence. The
national salvation movement by students was preceded
by a manifesto issued by professors of the various
universities at Peiping and was followed by the demons-
trations staged by students of various schools of the
same city. Subsequently, the movement was responded
to in every part of the country. All these indicate
the national spirit as well as the fact that the
national situation is in danger.
In view of the foregoing, the following
points strike us very forcibly:-
(1) In the past people paid much attention
to appeals regarding the national salvation movement; but
they overlooked practical efforts. Although the
shouting of slogans and the holding and staging of
processions and demonstrations can be really regarded
as signs of national spirit, yet they will not result
in any effective strength and will only give trouble-
makers an opportunity, unless such propaganda is
carried out along set principles and worked systematically.
At present the participants in the national
salvation movement are brilliant youths of the
educational circles. They ought certainly to be
ready to take strict precautions against those trouble-
makers and reactionary elements, because unless they
are very careful, there will be serious results.
We cannot forget the national situation of to-day, which
cannot be relieved by words only, but by hard efforts
effected by whole hearted action. The spirit and
strength of the people must be invoked in the salvation
of the nation and a long struggle is also necessitated,
so that the ridiculous "5-minute enthusiasm" will be
done away with.
(2) The Government should direct these
national salvation people carefully, who in turn should
observe good order and so save the national crisis
under the actual guidance of the Government. As the
participants in the national salvation movement are
students who are educated, they can be persuaded and
easily taught. In this way no illegal activities
by students will happen. Furthermore, they can be
easily directed how to support the Government.

December 18, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

(3) In the past national salvation movements
always aroused a misunderstanding among friendly nations.
In minor cases, the movements are regarded as
disturbances, but in major cases, as anti-foreign
activities. We are surprised to see such a misunder-
standing since the love and salvation of one's country
is the same in all other countries. Do the people
of other friendly nations not know that their respective
countries should be loved and that the national crisis
of their respective countries should be relieved? The
salvation of one's country is the obligation of the
people. Why should the people of China be an
exception? The Chinese people at heart have no
anti-foreign idea, and they have never rejected foreign
culture. We have no time to lose in welcoming
people of friendly nations who are rendering us mutual
benefits, but yet we have no anti-foreign ideas. The
Chinese people like peace and if friendly nations
can understand China, the reason for China's national
salvation movement will be clear to them.

The following resolutions were discussed and passed :-
(1) That the following measures be adopted to accelerate the future activities for national salvation :-
(a) To centralize the control of the various Students Unions of local universities for national salvation.
(b) To carry out a practical and permanent movement for national salvation.
(2) It was published in newspapers during the past few days that a federation known as the Federation of Local University Students For National Salvation had been inaugurated in Shanghai. The various local universities knew nothing about its establishment beforehand nor had they delegated any representatives to participate in the meetings held by this Federation. Moreover the Federation had failed to mention the place where the meetings were held and the names of the representatives who attended. It is evidently an illegal organization established under certain pretexts. It is therefore only reasonable that this Federation should not be recognised. It was decided:
(a) That a letter be sent to the local newspapers and news agencies denouncing the establishment of this Federation.
(b) That the local Tangpu and other political organs be requested to conduct investigations and to adopt strict measures to deal with such organizations.
(c) That the various Students Self-Control Unions and National Salvation Committees of the local Universities be instructed not to recognize such organizations.
(3) That the delegates of the various universities present write to the Secretary of the local University Students Federation asking him to convene a meeting of the representatives of the various local universities at the earliest date possible for the purpose of discussing measures for the unification of the local university students, so as to facilitate the adoption of a concentrated movement for national salvation.

Bureau of Education Advises Students to Refrain from Direct Action in their National Salvation Movements.

The Education Bureau yesterday sent the following letter to the Chinan ( 暨南 ), the Futan ( 復旦 ) and other universities and middle schools:-
"Although the situation in the North is tense, yet the foreign policy of our Government has already been ascertained. The Government will never inconsiderately allow, in any way, the losing of China's sovereign rights or the attempt to partitioning China's territory. The enthusiastic patriotism of the students of various schools and universities is worthy of respect; but at this time of national crisis, the holding and staging of processions and demonstrations will only result, in minor cases, in constituting an obstruction to the peace and order in the community and in major cases, in the creation of international trouble. It will of no benefit to either the nation or the people when our Government becomes definitely unable to deal with external affairs. All the opinions of teachers and students of various schools and universities may be written and offered to the Government for adoption, instead of their carrying out unworthy activities on account of intense indignation. We hereby hope that you will persuade the students to observe these instructions."

China Evening News (comment):

PATRIOTIC MOVEMENT

Since the May 4th movement, cases have rarely occurred wherein young students participated in the patriotic movement.
Subsequent to the outbreak of the North China affair, students at Peiping, moved by indignation, launched a patriotic movement.

                Students at Peiping

        On December 9, students at Peiping submitted
an appeal to the authorities protesting against the bogus

towards the students.

and Police Authorities.    The students were only holding
processions, and had submitted appeals against the
autonomous organization.    These were actions inspired by
patriotism.    The Peiping Authorities should have adopted
peaceful measures to stop the activities of the students

very cold weather and then arrested many of them.    We

to the Tientsin City Government, under the name of patriotism,
the Military and Police at Tientsin not only treated them
exceedingly well, but allowed the group to occupy the
offices of the authorities and to create uprisings.

occupy the offices of the authorities nor did they
create uprisings, nor was the action of their appeal
instigated by certain authorities, yet the Peiping
Authorities adopted a very different attitude towards them.
        Why did not the Military and Police
Authorities use water to sweep away the autonomous show
performed by the puppets?    Nevertheless, they have poured
water on the students who are opposed to such an autonomous
movement.    This is why the public are annoyed.
        The affairs at Peiping and Tientsin have
now reached a temporary settlement.    We hope that the
authorities will, in future, give concrete proof that
they are not less patriotic than the students.

AGITATION AGAINST THE AUTONOMOUS MOVEMENT IN NORTH CHINA.

The manifesto issued by educational circles
and the demonstration staged by university students of
Peiping have rekindled the national salvation spirit in
this locality which has been lying dormant for a number of
years.
To-day (December 12) about 300 important
members of the local educational, banking, bar and other
cultural bodies, headed by the Rev. Ma Siang Pah(馬相伯),
sent out a circular telegram to all the people throughout
the country, declaring that the settlement of the North China
and the North-East problems as local affairs will be refuted,
and suggesting the concentration of financial and military
strength to resist the enemy's invasion. The telegram
also requests the National Government to dispatch troops
to suppress the rebellious organizations in East Hopei and
the North-East.
The following is the text of the telegram:-
"Our national crisis is becoming more acute
daily. The four North-Eastern provinces have been annexed
and now the five provinces in North China are in danger.
If we deal with our enemy by bartering our land, our enemy
will not be satisfied unless all our land has been given up.
At the present juncture when our national existence is at
stake, our cultural circles, who are entrusted with the
mission of guiding the community, should no longer remain
calm and should immediately rise up and lead the masses to
engage in a national salvation movement. We warmly
support the 'last lesson' determination of our educational
circles of Peiping and the enthusiastic movement started
by the youths in North China for the salvation of their
country. We should make up our minds before the knives
of our enemy are laid to our necks. We should adopt
effective measures to preserve our national strength and
should struggle for the emancipation of our race. Events
which have occurred during the past four years convince
us that our enemy's aggression is not instigated by the
ambitions of a few of our enemies but is the natural trend
of the expansion of Imperialism. The acute economic
crisis and other factors have caused our enemies to pursue
their 'continental' policy. It will be tantamount to
asking a tiger for its skin if we still continue to
employ methods of compromise, co-operation and rapproche-
ment or parley, in an attempt to pacify our enemy.
"The struggle for the emancipation of the
people is not only the duty of the Chinese people, but also
the duty of all oppressed people. The greater the
oppression by our enemies, the stronger will be the
demand of the Chinese people for our emancipation. The
sole way to salvation for the Chinese people will be to
form as many people's bodies as possible and to fight
to the death. All intellectual people in the world will
sympathize with us deeply in such a sacred battle. A
weak policy will mean the dissolution of our race and will
only facilitate the enemy in our gradual extermination.

Chen Pao (Shanghai Morning Post, an official organ of
General Chiang Kai Shek) publishes the following editorial:-

FURTHER DISCUSSION OF THE HOPEI-CHARHAR QUESTION

In connection with the North China problem,
this paper has, on many occasions, exposed the important
nature of the situation and drawn the attention of the
Government and our readers to the subject. We hereby
bring up the subject for further discussion, being very
much alarmed by the reports in the local Japanese newspapers.
The formation of a Hopei-Charhar Political
Affairs Committee, which has been much talked about recently,
is an important matter. The Japanese newspapers have
stated that the Hopei-Charhar Political Affairs Committee
will be an organization such that it in reality constitutes
a separation from the National Government in spite of the
fact that the members of the Committee will be appointed
by the National Government, and that the full authority
for military, diplomatic, financial and communication
affairs in the district as well as the appointing and
discharging of officials comes under the power of the
Committee itself. We are quite sure that the National
Government will never permit the formation of such a
peculiar political affairs committee in China. Meanwhile
we hope that our people will understand the object of
"certain" authorities, and become aware of the grave
nature of the situation of China.
The Japanese newspapers are hostile towards
the opposition by educationists in Peiping and Tientsin
to the secession movement in China and towards the appeal
made by students in Peiping for the punishment of traitors.
They thought that all these activities had been instigated
by the Chinese Kuomintang and Europeans and American
people and that they are anti-Japanese. The Japanese
newspapers declare that the Japanese Embassy has requested
the Japanese Foreign Office to lodge a protest with the
National Government. From this, it will be seen that
the Japanese Authorities desire the National Government
to prohibit the appearance of any actions in China which
aim at opposing any secession movement. Movements
struggling for the existence of the nation should not be
interferred with by foreign influence. The work for
good relations with neighbouring countries is not the
one-sided obligation of the Chinese people. If anybody
works for the separation of our country with the left hand,
and forbids actions to preserve the existence of our
country with the right hand, all we can do is to reject
such activities.
The Hopei-Charhar Political Affairs Committee
has yet to be formed, yet the Japanese newspapers have
circulated reports that the Chinese Kuomintang will be
driven away from North China. From this, we should
realize the real intention of "certain" authorities.
The Japanese newspapers nowadays publish as
much anti-Chinese comments and news as possible in order
to strengthen the minds of the Japanese to expel and
insult China, thereby causing the relations between China
and Japan to become worse. In the event of such things
being allowed to go on, the so-called friendship and
rapprochement between China and Japan will never materialize.

Chen Pao (Shanghai Morning Post, an official organ of
General Chiang Kai Shek) publishes the following editorial:-

HOPEI AND CHARHAR PROVINCES

In connection with the situation in North
China, it is reported that a so-called Hopei & Charhar
Political Affairs Committee will be established in Peiping.
Prominent Chinese persons in retirement will be invited
to serve on the Committee. We are of the opinion that
the National Government must pay careful consideration
to this question.
Will not such an organization as the so-called
Hopei & Charhar Political Affairs Committee constitute a
menace to the integrity of the territory of China and be
detrimental to the ruling power of the National Government?
An observation of the statements made by responsible
officials in North China shows that their movements do
not mean that they would separate from China, thereby
it would not impair the integrity of China's territory.
Judging from facts, the consequence of the formation of
such an organization can hardly avert a menace to the
integrity of the territory of China. What foreigners
are eager for, day and night, is that more independent
units should be existed in China so as to make them oppose
one another. Separate arrangements will then be made
with these independent units by means of coercion and
promises. By so doing, the great desire of their
aggressive policy can be achieved. The Chinese
Government is now expected to form such an organization
voluntarily and this will meet the desire of ambitious
countries and will prove exceptionally convenient to
them for encroaching upon China in future. Although
the presence of such an organization in China may not
cause any trouble for some time, yet the Chinese Government
will repent when it is too late. Regarding his activities
in East Hopei, Yin Zu Keng has also declared that his
action does not mean a secession from China Proper, but
it is known to all that Yin is securing shelter from
the Japanese. Hopei and Charhar are two important
boundary outposts of China. How can such an organization
be established in these two provinces as a precedent?
If such a special organization can be established in
Hopei and Charhar, then the same can be formed in Shansi
and Shantung when China is further oppressed and threatened
by Japan. In the event of the Japanese demanding the
formation of such an organization in Fukien, Chekiang and
other vicinities in future, on what grounds will China
reject the demand? China will thus suffer terribly.
The question relating to Hopei and Charhar is whether
or not these two provinces are still subject to the control
of the National Government. Putting it another way,
is it possible for the National Government to exercise
authority in these two provinces? The so-called Hopei
& Charhar Political Affairs Committee will only become
an extraordinary organization which will separate from
China should the National Government not be in a position
to exercise its authority there. The Government must
give careful consideration to this matter.

Chen Pao (Shanghai Morning Post, an official organ of
General Chiang Kai Shek) publishes the following editorials-

THE NORTH CHINA QUESTION

The people of China are the best lovers of
peace in the world. The 5th National Conference of the
Kuomintang has clearly announced that the National
Government will not give up striving for peace until it
is hopeless. In consequence of this, whether or not the
peace in the Far East or in the whole world can be
maintained will depend entirely upon our neighbouring
country. Despite the activities of high Chinese officials
presenting suggestions for peace, no approval whatever
has yet been obtained from the other side.
China is a weak, backward and invaded country
and she is eagerly desirous of peace. There is, however,
a certain limit for peace, that is to say, the people of
China have all come to see that the discussion for peace
must be based on the principle that "the integrity of the
national territory must be ensured and China's sovereign
rights must be made complete". On the contrary, if the
negotiations for peace are handled in a manner that will
cause our national territory to be separated or that will
lead to the violation of the national sovereign rights,
then the stage is come when peace is hopeless.
Taking the present chance when there is still
some slight hope for the peace of the Far East, we now
wish to give a frank talk to our friendly neighbouring
country and to the National Government as follows:-
The intelligent people of our friendly neighbouring
country should consider the relations between China and
Japan closely and devise peaceful measures for the mutual
existence of the two nations. Before the Meiji Regime of
Japan, Japan had to recognize that she had a history of
some three thousand years as part of the Chinese race.
Japan received nearly all her civilization from China.
However, after adopting Western civilization, Japan began
to learn, in the ways of the West, how to oppress the weak.
She annexed the Liuchu Islands, obtained Taiwan and took
Korea. The Japanese were still not satisfied with that,
and seized China's Four North-Eastern Provinces during
the September 18 Incident. The Woosung-Shanghai Pact
and the Tengku Agreement were subsequently signed. Japan
has now initiated the so-called "North China Autonomous
Movement" as if China had not yet sustained the gravest
insults. In the opinion of Japan formerly, Japan would
have failed to carry on without Manchuria. Now, Japan
is of the opinion that she cannot ensure the safety of
Manchuria unless she is in control of North China. Will
Japan be satisfied when she has obtained North China?
It is to be feared that in only a few months, Japan will
hold the view that she cannot ensure the safety of North
China without seizing the Yangtze Valley. In this manner,
what will become of China? There is a proverb that "even
a worm will turn". Will not China become a worm or will
she not become a second Abyssinia? It is said that a
Confucius temple has been established in Japan and the
descendants of that Sage were some time ago invited to go
to Japan to participate in the ceremony of the inauguration

December 6, 1935.
Afternoon Translation.

of the temple. The Japanese have also preached the so-called doctrine of justice in the bogus state of Manchukuo. Yet all these actions of the Japanese will mean that at best, Japan will become a conqueror of the world. However, such a conqueror will not last long. It is natural that China will suffer heavily should she fight, but it is not quite sure that Japan will be completely safe. We hope Japanese intelligent people will be broad-minded and so save the present dangerous situation.

The Chinese Government must realize the necessary conditions for peace. It must, first of all, draw up schemes to cope with the national affairs. It should give permission whenever it is possible, but reject any demand which is impossible to accept. It should not hesitate to deal with anything. It must be determined to sacrifice all in order to obtain true peace. At this time when there is still some hope for peace, the Government must select high class diplomatic officials to announce the sincerity of the Government to be friendly with neighbouring countries and to draw the attention of foreign countries to the Sino-Japanese affairs. The people throughout the country must consolidate and be prepared to sacrifice everything for the sake of our race and country when it appears that there is no longer any hope of peace.

Regarding the North China question, the officials engaged in this connection must take particular care in their mission. If we engage Chinese, who are well versed with Japanese affairs, to effect the cancellation of the East Hopei Autonomous Committee inaugurated by Yin Zu Keng, who is illegally communicating with Japan, and form a Committee to be placed ostensibly under the control of the Chinese Government but in reality under the direction of persons behind the stage, it will not be a true peace and will only cause the country to lose more territory.
