Journal de Shanghai :

INTERVIEW WITH PRESIDENT OF "AUTONOMOUS COUNCIL OF EAST HOPEI".

Yin Jou Keng, Inspector of the Demilitarized Area in Hopei Province, proclaimed the autonomy of Luntung on November 24 and has since become the President of the "Autonomy Council of East Hopei."
The following interview took place between Yin Jou Keng and Mr. Alphonse Monastier, editor of the French newspaper "Politique de Pekin" :-
Q: We have heard of the formation of the new Council of which you are the President. We have come to seek information from you at first hand.
A: I shall explain to you my object. I am fighting not the country but the Kuomintang for the Kuomintang has been ruining the country during the past 25 years. I would like to see China return to the same state that she was in in the year 1911. I have seen service with the Kuomintang in the hope of ameliorating somewhat the consequences of its acts but without success. Recently I sent to Nanking an appeal that the period of political tutelage be terminated for it is only another form of dictatorship, and to establish a Constitutional Government. The Fifth National Congress was still in session then. Generals Sung Cheh Yuan and Han Fu Chu also sent similar telegrams. To my disappointment, Nanking ignored our advice. Instead, Nanking decreed the nationalization of silver. Thereafter, I hesitated no longer and launched the present autonomous movement. This movement is principally directed against the Kuomintang. If the Kuomintang can be driven away from the whole country it will bring much happiness to the people.

December 4, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

Q: What steps have you taken since the day of the proclamation?
A: After my telegram of protest to Nanking, I sent a telegram of explanation to the people and to Generals Sung Cheh Yuan, Chang Sheng, Han Fu Chu and Tsino Chen Yin and another telegram informing the Legations of the various powers in China.
Q: The foreign powers may not have much to say for the time being, but don't you think that Japan will be alarmed for the movement involves the demilitarized area and jeopardizes the Tangku Armistice?
A: Japan understands the meaning of the movement; it depends upon the people. She is following the movement with sympathetic attention.
Q: Are you not afraid of a reaction at Nanking? Is it not being said that Nanking is concentrating troops in Honan?
A: I am ready for fighting. The Government should think twice before attempting to suppress the movement. Besides, it would have already taken action had it been really disposed to do so.
Q: Perhaps it is waiting for a more favourable movement. You know that Nanking is ready to reach an understanding with Tokyo to bring about a settlement of the Sino-Japanese question. The Chinese Charge d'Affaires at Tokyo has informed Mr. Shigemitsu, the Japanese Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs, that his Government is ready to open negotiations with Tokyo and that it had designated General Chiang Tso Ping to undertake the negotiations.
A: Whatever Nanking may do and supposing even that an arrangement is come to between Nanking and Tokyo, I, for my part, will continue to maintain the autonomous government.
Q: Are you certain that you have sufficient supporters around you?
A: I have the best grounds for believing that I shall find all the help I shall need from the authorities of the five northern provinces.
Q: Did you see General Sung Cheh Yuan yesterday when he passed here?
A: No. Yesterday I received a visit from General Sui, Chief of the 9th Brigade of the 29th Army who congratulated me and, on the orders of General Sung Cheh Yuan, placed his troops at my disposal.
Q: What was the cause of the first failure of the movement?
A: There was no failure, the movement had only been retarded because of certain circumstances.
Q: What do you think of the movement in Tientsin?
A: It is a spontaneous movement of the people in sympathy with ours.
Q: Do you think there will be a similar movement in Peiping?
A: If the authorities are slow to move, it is possible a people's demonstration may occur.
Q: General Dohara returned to Peiping yesterday. Do you know the reason for his return?
A: He has come to take stock of the present situation. I have not seen him but I have met him before at Peiping and Tientsin.

December 4, 1935.
Afternoon Translation.

Q: Supposing, however, that the movement is
confined to the area which is under your jurisdiction
and that, for some reason or other, the authorities of
the other northern provinces do not fall in line with you,
would you proceed with the organization of the political
statute of East Hopei?
A: All the districts are united under my
presidency. We shall continue as before without reference
to Nanking. In short, the following are my aims:-
1) I am seceding from the Kuomintang but not from China.
2) I shall accept full responsibility for civil, political
and diplomatic affairs throughout the whole area of
East Hopei.
3) I shall respect the International treaties.
4) I shall give an undertaking to protect the lives and
property of foreigners.
5) I shall endeavour to rally around me the authorities
of the other provinces so that the whole country may
enjoy peace.
Q: Do you propose to take special measures against
the Communists and will you work in co-operation with Japan
and Manchukuo in this respect?
A: The Communist danger is not imminent. For the
present, we know how to deal with it with our own efforts.
Later, we shall see.
Q: I have seen your manifesto. Supposing that
Nanking takes action against you because of this manifesto?
A: I repeat: I am not afraid to fight. I have
been undertaking this revolutionary work for ten years and
it has now been crowned with success. I was by the side
of General Koo Tsong Lin on November 24, 1925, when he
rebelled against Marshal Chang Tso Lin. It is to mark
the continuity of my work that I selected the date of
November 24 to issue my manifesto.

JAPANESE SOLDIERS DETAIN TRAINS OF THE TIENTSIN-PUKOW RAILWAY
At 10 a.m. November 27, some 40 Japanese soldiers led by their officers arrived at the Tientsin-Pukow Railway Station in an armoured car and three freight wagons. They entered the Station Master's room and requested the Master to refrain from issuing the "all clear batons" to the trains coming to the south. Japanese soldiers were sent to watch the starting of the 75th train to Tsinan. Other Japanese soldiers proceeded to the Western Station of the Tientsin-Pukow Railway by motor cars and prevented the 21st passenger train from proceeding further. At the same time, the Peiping-Liaoning Railway Administration also received a telephonic report from Foong Tan stating that some 60 Japanese soldiers arrived at 5.50 a.m, bringing a field gun with them and had mounted guard of the station, watched the Station Master and prevented the freight train from proceeding south.
Loh Meng Hsiung (罗孟雄), Assistant Manager of the Peiping-Liaoning Railway Administration, called on Tada, Commander of the Japanese Military Headquarters at Tientsin and opened negotiations over the matter. At 12.15 p.m. November 27, the Japanese soldiers began to withdraw from the Chief Station and the Western Station of the Tientsin-Pukow Railway and drove away all the trains in the station.
At 10 a.m. November 27, the officers of the Tientsin-Pukow Railway called on Tada, Japanese Military Commander in Tientsin, in connection with the detention of trains by the Japanese soldiers. The two parties verbally agreed to the following conditions:-
1) No empty trains should be sent to the south.
2) Troops should not be transported by trains.
3) When a train proceeds to the south, a train should go to the north at the same time.
On November 26, a party of Japanese soldiers and of Peace Preservation Corps under the command of Chang Ching Yue entered Ning Ho (宁河) and took over the control of the Hsien Government by force. The Magistrate was driven away. The Hsien district is now included in the bogus organization.

The Suppression of Rebels

The activities of rebels, such as Yin Zu Keng, Shih You San and Zee Sih Yuen, have increased the instability in the North. Although the National Government has ordered the arrest of Yin Zu Keng and appointed General Ho Yin Ching Superior Officer of the Executive Yuan at Peiping, we cannot hold optimistic views towards the situation in the North until the Government has resorted to military action to suppress the rebels. The reason why the rebels have been so bold as to create a disturbance in the North is

AUTONOMY MOVEMENT IN NORTH CHINA - REBELS STAGE
DEMONSTRATIONS IN TIENTSIN.

At 6 a.m. November 25 the rebel elements hiding
in the certain Concession assembled several hundred of their
number, some wearing uniforms or armlets with inscriptions
"North China People's Self-Defence Corps", and others
carrying clubs and two machine guns, who proceeded in trucks

gun posts in the street, they proceeded to the City
Government in several batches, either on foot or in trucks,

At 8.40 a.m. the first batch of rebels, numbering
about 60, drove up in two trucks before the City Government
and, claiming themselves to be members of the People's Self-
Defence Corps, requested for an interview with the Mayor.
As Mayor Chen Kuh was not present, they were received by

submitted a petition demanding the abdication of the
government. Mr. Sung promised to transmit the petition
to the Mayor, after which those in plainclothes left but
those in uniforms remained in the building. Upon a
telephonic message from Mr. Sung, Ikegami, Chief of the

At 9 a.m. a second batch of rebels, about 100
in number, the majority of whom were boys, arrived and

the "North China Farmers Self-Salvation Corps". They were
persuaded to leave by the Chief Secretary, Mr. Sung Zung Yue.
At about 10 a.m. another batch of rebels,
numbering about 200, wearing plainclothes and uniforms,

be the "Chong Hsien People's Self-Defence Corps".
At 11 a.m. the demonstrators assembled in front

Commissioner and shouted slogans. The Headquarters
immediately called out an armed guard commanded by Adjutant

daily. There were also a few persons of a certain
nationality who took part in the movement.

NICHI-NICHI

ARRIVAL OF RELIEF MARINES FROM JAPAN.

About 200 Japanese Marines
arrived yesterday on the S. S. Shanghai Maru to take the
place of others who have already completed their terms
of service in Shanghai.

53 JAPANESE ANARCHISTS ARRESTED IN JAPAN.

It is reported that recently
the Tokyo Police arrested 53 important anarchists,
including Uemura, age 29, chairman of the Central
Committee of the Japanese Anarchistic Communist Party,
Aizawa, their chief secretary, Futami, chief of their
Finance Section and Irie, chief of their Military Section.
According to information given by the prisoners to the
Police there are about 400 anarchists in Japan.
The Tokyo Police issued
instructions to the police authorities in Yokohama, Kobe,
Moji and Nagasaki to keep a close watch on anarchists
who try to go to Shanghai and other foreign ports.

JIPPO

JAPANESE MILITARY AUTHORITIES' DECISION REGARDING
JAPAN'S POLICY TOWARDS CHINA.

A Dentsu telegram from Kagoshima
dated November 18 states that as a result of a conference
held between War Minister and General Imai, chief of the
Military Affairs Bureau, to discuss the China policy
question, the following decisions have arrived at:-
1. Following the Nanking incident the anti-Japanese
attitude of the important officials of the Nanking Govern-
ment has become stronger. The Japanese Government should
take speedy and appropriate measures according to the
pre-determined policy towards China.
2. The policy towards the North has already been
adopted and the Kwantung Army Commanders Headquarters have
been instructed regarding the policy. For this reason
the War Ministry should seek the co-operation of the
Japanese authorities there. In this connection the
understanding of the government organs concerned is
necessary. The War Minister will, therefore, make
appropriate arrangements with the Premier and the Finance
Minister.

JAPAN OPPOSES MILITARY SUPPRESSION IN THE NORTH

A Dentsu telegram from Hsinking
dated November 17 reports that the Kwantung Army pays
serious attention to the autonomy movement in the North.
If Chiang Kai Shek sends troops to the North to suppress
the autonomy movement violating the Tangku Truce and the
Boxer Agreement, the Kwantung Army will put a stop to
the Chinese military interference in the movement.

November 18, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pao published the following telegrams from
Tientsin on November 17 :-

GENERAL DOIHARA DIRECTS THE AUTONOMOUS MOVEMENT IN
NORTH CHINA

According to information from a reliable
source, General Doihara of the Japanese Kwantung Army on
November 7 submitted a demand to General Sung Cheh Yuan,
the Garisson Commander of Peiping and Tientsin, requesting
him to proceed with the movement for an autonomy in North
China, within three days. General Sung, however, replied
that this cannot be decided on, until the 5th National
Congress of the Kuomintang, at present being held in
Nanking, is over.
It is said that the various offices of
the National Government in North China, including the
Peiping Military Council, will be abolished while a new
organ will be established with General Sung Cheh Yuan as
the leader. The new organ will, however, maintain some
adequate connections with the National Government. This
is the fundamental scheme of the formation of an autonomous
government in North China but whether the National
Government will accept it or not is at present unknown.
The above information has been released by
Japan and is reported to have been confirmed by the
Chinese authorities.
It is further reported that the Customs
revenue, the Salt revenue, Consolidated Tax, Stamp Tax,
and other government revenues of North China will be with-
held for the development of North China.
General Doihara is intending to make North
China entirely independent from the National Government
and proposes that the suggested autonomous government
adopts a new emblem and new coins. General Sung Cheh
Yuan, however, is insisting that (1) the new government
should be under the National Government in its organization
and (2) the integrity of North China should be preserved;
none of North China should be annexed by Japan or "Manchukuo".
According to general observation, the "connections" between
the suggested autonomous government and the National
Government may be cut off at a time when the National
Government may be alleged to have undertaken anti-Japanese
activities.
General Sung Cheh Yuan held that this
movement should not be carried until the time is opportune
and has requested Japan accordingly. The latter, however,
is exerting every effort to press Sung.
The so-called new state of North China
would consist of Hopei, Charhar, Suiyuan, Shansi and
Shantung Provinces. It has not been definitely decided
however, whether or not the two last named provinces will
be included.
